API mode

API mode: the Codex app runs its own signed engine and uses the gateway only as a model provider, so its app tools work on gateway models.

About 8 min read · 8 sections

On this page
01 Why it exists 02 What API mode changes 03 The flow 04 The switch, and what is held back 05 What API mode gives up 06 Using it 07 Telemetry 08 Verification status, 2026-10-25

API mode is an opt-in desktop setup. The ChatGPT app starts its own signed Codex engine and keeps every one of its own tools, and GateFox serves that engine as a plain Responses model provider. There is no adapter between them.

Adapter mode (default)                    API mode
ChatGPT.app                               ChatGPT.app
  └─ engine  ← CODEX_CLI_PATH wrapper       └─ its own signed engine
       └─ gateway shim ── translation            └─ config: model_provider = "harness_gateway"
            └─ provider inference                     └─ base_url = http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1
app tools: unavailable                    app tools: available on every gateway model

Why it exists

The app's codex_app tools (automation_update, create_thread, …) reach the app through a pipe that only trusts an OpenAI-signed engine process chain. The adapter is an unsigned Node process sitting in that chain, so with the adapter in place those tools are out of reach no matter what the model asks for. Client tool reachability covers the wider question of which tools a client can see on a gateway model; this is the one class of tools the adapter cannot reach at all, because the boundary is process signing rather than tool exposure.

What API mode changes

gateway desktop api-mode on writes four things into the native Codex configuration, and nothing else:

Key Value
model_providers.harness_gateway this gateway: loopback /v1, wire_api = "responses", no websockets, 2 retries, 90 s idle timeout, and the gateway token helper as its auth command
model_provider harness_gateway
model_catalog_json <state>/api-mode-models.json, this gateway's model list
model --model, else the model already in use when the gateway serves it, else the first listed row

Every model goes through that provider, GPT included. A native catalog row cannot name a provider, so a row that bypassed the gateway would be the only model in the picker that the gateway is not serving — and the whole point is one model list with one set of tools. off puts back exactly what on found, key by key, and clears the ones that were absent.

Storing the gateway's provider and catalog file in the user's own config.toml is a deliberate exception to the rule the adapter follows for native configuration writes (app-server, enforced in src/app-server-config-writes.ts). That rule exists because adapter rows only live as long as the adapter runs, so a saved gateway model would break the next plain Codex start. In API mode the rows are the point and they are permanent by design — which is also why the receipt exists and why off must run before that configuration is anyone else's problem.

The flow

flowchart TD
  A["gateway desktop api-mode on"] --> B{ChatGPT running?}
  B -- yes --> R1[refuse: quit it first]
  B -- no --> C{receipt exists?}
  C -- yes --> R2[refuse: already on]
  C -- no --> D{CODEX_CLI_PATH foreign?}
  D -- yes --> R3[refuse: nothing written]
  D -- no --> E[read native config<br/>through the app's engine]
  E --> F[write api-mode-models.json]
  F --> G[write api-mode.json receipt]
  G --> H[one config/batchWrite<br/>guarded by expectedVersion]
  H --> I[unsetenv CODEX_CLI_PATH<br/>only if it was our wrapper]
  I --> J[next app launch: own engine, gateway provider]
  H -. failure .-> K[restore originals, delete receipt, rethrow]

The engine does the editing. gateway desktop api-mode starts ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex-cli/bin/codex app-server --listen stdio:// with CODEX_HOME pointed at the native home, initializes as harness_gateway_api_mode with the experimental API, and uses config/read and config/batchWrite. It never parses or rewrites config.toml itself, so comments, key order and every setting the gateway does not own come back untouched. Each write carries the expectedVersion the read reported, so a configuration edited meanwhile fails instead of being clobbered. A key is cleared by writing null, which the engine's own writer removes.

The switch, and what is held back

<state>/api-mode.json (mode 0600) is the only thing that distinguishes API mode from the adapter on a machine:

{ "version": 1, "nativeHome": "/Users/you/.codex",
  "original": { "model": "gpt-5.1" }, "providerTableExisted": false,
  "applied": { "provider": "harness_gateway", "catalogPath": "<state>/api-mode-models.json", "model": "codex/gpt-6.1-sol" },
  "cliPathCleared": true, "enabledAt": "2026-10-25T10:00:00Z" }

original records presence and value of the three user-layer keys API mode moves, so an absent key goes back absent rather than empty. It is written before the batch write, so a crash in between leaves the record that says what to undo; off removes it last.

While it exists, every path that would arm the adapter stands down. The daemon's first-step launchctl setenv preset and the service's desktop-restore child skip and record one desktop_api_mode event (action: "preset", outcome: "skipped") per process; a hand-run gateway desktop register refuses. The preset's receipt check and its setter share the registration lock with on and off, and it checks again while holding that lock. The standalone login-environment script calls the same locked preset after its receipt check, so a concurrent on cannot slip a setenv between those steps; on upgrades an existing gateway-owned script with that guard and refuses an older direct-launchctl agent until it is re-registered. The desktop registration receipt and the service plan are not changed: API mode only takes CODEX_CLI_PATH out of the login session, and only when the session's value was one of this gateway's own wrappers. A foreign override is refused before anything is written, because API mode could not hand it back. gateway desktop api-mode status reports this as cliPathOverride: "gateway"|"none"|"other", never the path itself.

If an on batch is rejected before the engine applies it, API mode retires only its pre-write receipt. For an uncertain result, it re-reads the user layer and restores only keys still equal to API mode's values; it restores or removes a provider table only when it still exactly equals the table API mode wrote. A failed restoration keeps the receipt and reports desktop_api_mode as failed with the fixed rollback reason, so the adapter stays guarded and off can retry safely.

The catalog stays current without a timer or another background item: the running service rewrites it at the moment it adopts a new gateway configuration, and only while the receipt exists. A model added to the gateway is written to that catalog for the next engine reload. Immediate refresh of an already-open model picker has not been verified.

What API mode gives up

Lost beside adapter mode Why
Shared executor survival No adapter means no gateway-owned engine: quitting the app or losing its connection ends the chat's execution, and the SSH/durable-chat paths that lean on the shared executor are not in play.
Gateway SDK patches The deferred-tool fallback in scripts/patches/gateway-dynamic-tools.patch and the rest of the pinned gateway SDK never load, so a caller-declared deferred tool on a model without tool search stays hidden.
Adapter compaction, effort and tier handling Adapter-side compaction, reasoning-effort translation and service-tier selection happen in the shim; API mode sends whatever the app's own engine sends.
A mixed native + gateway model list The adapter merges the native catalog with the gateway's rows. API mode replaces the list with the gateway's rows only: model_catalog_json can point at one file, and a native row cannot name the gateway provider.
The gateway's own chat identity Rows are plain provider rows; the account-scoped naming and classification the adapter records do not apply.

Keep the adapter for shared executors, durable chats, SSH and the patched SDK. Choose API mode when an app feature that only exists as a codex_app tool matters more.

Using it

gateway desktop api-mode on                  # macOS, gateway running here, ChatGPT quit
gateway desktop api-mode on --model ALIAS    # a specific row from `gateway catalog`
gateway desktop api-mode status
gateway desktop api-mode off

Quit ChatGPT (Command-Q) first: both on and off refuse while it is running, because the configuration only takes effect at the next launch. off then restores the native configuration and re-arms the adapter through the same preset the service uses, so the next launch is back in adapter mode. It reports cliPathRestored: false with a fixed cliPathRestoreReason when that preset skips or fails. A clientOnly gateway refuses on — API mode needs a gateway running on this Mac.

scripts/e2e-api-mode-native-config.mjs runs the real on/off logic against the app's real signed engine in a throwaway native home and checks the resulting config.toml round trip. It never launches the app and never touches a login session.

Telemetry

One event, desktop_api_mode, with exactly action (on, off, preset), outcome (applied, refused, rolled_back, failed, skipped) and a fixed reason when there is one. No path, model, configuration value or environment value is ever recorded. See diagnostics.

Verification status, 2026-10-25

The native configuration check passed against the signed app engine, including restoring comments, absent keys and user changes. On macbook-server an isolated API-mode enable and disable also completed, and the test app and its temporary home were removed afterwards. The normal gateway desktop registration remained active.

A previous direct-engine trial exposed automation_update to a gateway-model chat and showed the app's normal approval prompt. Saving and firing a real schedule remain unverified: that trial received invalid model arguments, and the latest attempt was blocked by the desktop lock screen before a prompt was sent. API mode has not been enabled in the user's normal Codex home or deployed as a new release.
